title: The “Made in Europe” label is wearing thin while Asia does the stitching
gist: EU origin rules let luxury houses label products Made in Europe after minimal final operations while Asia does primary manufacturing; court probes and new due-diligence rules threaten the heritage narrative as Asian consumers drift toward local brands.

insights.claim: Under Article 60(2) of the EU Customs Code a product can carry a 'Made in' label if its last substantial transformation occurs in that country, letting brands do primary manufacturing in Asia and minimal final steps in Europe, with oversight relying largely on self-declaration.
insights.speaker: Sjenica Sevilla
insights.so_what: Origin labelling gives little real assurance; regulatory tightening is a reputational risk for luxury.
insights.locator: This tension stems from international trade regulations

insights.claim: A 2024 Milan prosecutors' probe found illegal subcontractor networks in Lombardy and Tuscany supplying houses including Dior and Armani, with Chinese-owned facilities making bags for under EUR100 that sold for thousands.
insights.speaker: Sjenica Sevilla
insights.so_what: Supply-chain labour-abuse cases are a recurring legal and brand risk for luxury groups.

insights.claim: European luxury relies on advanced Asian industrial and artisanal capabilities, including Chinese technical processing and Indian embroidery ateliers such as Chanakya International supplying Dior, Fendi, Lanvin and Valentino.
insights.speaker: Sjenica Sevilla
insights.so_what: Asian suppliers have more bargaining power and capability than the low-skill narrative implies.
insights.locator: At the same time, the narrative

insights.claim: Younger East and Southeast Asian consumers show logo fatigue and growing willingness to substitute regional designers for European heritage brands, exemplified by China's Guochao movement.
insights.speaker: Sjenica Sevilla
insights.so_what: Risk to European luxury demand in Asia as local brands gain credibility.

insights.claim: The EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, being phased in, aims to mandate supply chain traceability and narrow the gap between prestige storytelling and manufacturing reality.
insights.speaker: Sjenica Sevilla
insights.so_what: Compliance cost and disclosure risk for European luxury groups.
